components.control: Advanced Collapse holding the URL TextInput, Restart Button and auto-start Switch
components.rejected: Always-visible URL (rank inversion — the managed server needs no address); a second tab (one group, not a destination)
components.why: Collapse hides server machinery most users need only when something breaks — progressive disclosure with the ApiKeySection precedent.

components.control: Capability, safety and example Text lines above the fold
components.rejected: A help link (leaves the surface; the safety contract must be read, not fetched)
components.why: Recognition over recall: the tab teaches what to say and why it is safe before anything breaks, and Text is the map's body-copy control.

components.control: Single Button 'Test connection' beside Status; Restart inside Advanced
components.rejected: Two peer buttons (which-fixes-my-problem is a real decision); icon-only refresh (the action deserves a word)
components.why: One visible action ends the Test-vs-Restart dilemma; Restart is recovery, so it lives with the failure it recovers from.

components.control: Approve/Decline Button pair on the mirrored pending approval
components.rejected: Tap-only (excludes keyboard and screen-reader users by construction); global Y/N hotkeys (steal keys from the app being typed in)
components.why: The keyboard and screen-reader path to the pill's tap — same POST approve, no time limit, because a click causes something to happen.

components.control: Switch 'Start agent with Parley', inside Advanced
components.rejected: Always-on with no out (no way to debug a toxic server); a Checkbox beside a save button (there is none)
components.why: The change takes effect on next launch, which from the user's view is immediate — the map's Switch Use-when.

components.rejected: Bare Text (no status semantics; the Overview already reads badges as state)
components.why: Matches the Overview's Missing/Stored key badges, so agent state reads the same as key state.

components.control: Alert for a failed spawn, test, restart or run
components.rejected: Toast (leaves on a timer; the failure must persist until fixed)
components.why: Component-selection: standing region state is an Alert, and the message sits beside the button that produced it.

components.control: One-line capability summary; per-server Text rows with Badge counts inside Advanced
components.rejected: Full server list above the fold (grows into a devops dashboard); Switches (would promise control Parley does not have)
components.why: Health is display-only: one line proves reachability at a glance, per-server rows exist for diagnosis.

components.control: Select row 'Act key' in the Gesture tab
components.rejected: SegmentedControl (eight gesture keys will not fit in segments)
components.why: The dictate, edit and explain rows beside it are Selects; consistency inside the group beats the jsdom cost.

components.control: SettingRow 'Agent' with a badge in the Overview Status group
components.rejected: A rail badge (the rail carries identity, not state)
components.why: Status is the readiness surface, and the row jumps to the Agent tab the way the key rows open their forms. Starting gets a third, non-error badge treatment, and agent state never enters the ready computation — dictation readiness is independent.

components.control: The orb Notice (message + hint, no buttons) for progress, confirm and result
components.rejected: A settings Modal (wrong window, steals focus); a toast (cannot hold a decision)
components.why: The pill is the only surface visible inside another app, and tap-the-key confirm matches the word offer — Enter does not belong to Parley.

nonGoals: MCP servers configured in Parley — they live in the Mastra project's MCPClient config.
Hot-reloading the shipped server — dev spawns mastra dev in the sibling checkout, packaged spawns the bundle built by scripts/build-agent.sh.
Memory across runs — one thread per run; the agent may add memory later without Parley changing.
An agent picker — one agent, parley-action.
Conversational follow-up turns — 'book it for Tuesday' with no antecedent gets best-effort-or-decline, not a clarifying question.
Voice approval ('say yes') — tap and the tab buttons are the v1 paths; spoken approval is the follow-up.
Agent auth on localhost — accepted v1 risk; any local process can POST runs. Token later.
Elicitation forms on the Parley side — approvals are one-line summaries with a tap, not questionnaires.
TTS read-back of results — long answers go to the clipboard.
First-run wizard changes — Agent stays a settings tab, as Deepgram did.
Fallback to another agent when one fails.
feature.problem: Parley hears and pastes, rewrites and explains — but it cannot do. Someone who says 'book dentist Tuesday 9am' gets text in a field, not an appointment. This feature hands the command to an agent instead of answering it inline: a fourth gesture key transcribes the speech and POSTs it to a Mastra agent in a new parley-agent project, which plans and acts through its own MCP servers. Progress streams back over SSE onto the pill, each destructive tool suspends into a one-tap pill approval, and the result lands as one line — or on the clipboard when it is long. Approvals wait until answered and say what happens if you do nothing: only an explicit tap runs, Esc or a new command cancels. The Agent tab leads with capability and the safety contract, with server machinery under Advanced. Parley starts the server itself on launch and supervises it: dev spawns mastra dev in the sibling checkout, packaged spawns the bundled build, an already-answering port is attached to instead of double-spawned, crashes restart three times before the tab says offline, and the gesture blocks with directions while the agent is down. Failures are named and first-class: classified spawn errors, reconnect-by-status, stale events dropped by run and sequence, cancels that kill suspended runs, a standing record of every failure, and a graceful quit. Frame note: the settings window is not PageShell and the pill is a canvas overlay, so both archetypes below are illustrative and not probe-enforced, as in parley-007 to parley-012.

surfaces.name: Agent tab · Connection
surfaces.purpose: Shows the agent is on, what voice commands can reach, and the safety contract — server machinery waits under Advanced.

states.empty: The server has not answered yet. Parley starts it on launch; if this never clears, the error names the failure.
states.error: A failed spawn, test, restart or run names the failure beside the button ('agent project not found at …', 'port busy — something else holds :4111'); the old URL stays until a test passes.
states.loading: Settings resolve before the shell mounts, as today. Test connection spins its own button; the server list never skeletons.
states.success: A reachable agent shows Online with its capability line; the Overview Agent row flips to match. A waiting approval or live run shows as a read-only row; failures persist as an Alert until the next run.

surfaces.name: Act run · pill notices

rows: Tap Right Shift to run · Esc cancels
panels.title: Delete 3 events?

surfaces.purpose: Progress, approvals and answers happen in the pill: Parley never steals focus mid-run.

states.empty: Nothing to confirm: the agent answered from reads, or it is unreachable — in which case the gesture was blocked before listening.
states.error: The run failed: a red notice names it — 'Agent failed · timeout'. Details and the fix survive in Settings › Agent.
states.loading: The agent is working: the pill wears the act hue and the notice carries its latest step — 'Checking calendar…'. Past 60 s the pill collapses to a dot until the next step, approval or result.
states.success: Done in one line — 'Deleted 3 events'. Answers over ~120 chars go to the clipboard and the notice says 'Copied — paste anywhere'.
